etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 御 (o, honorific prefix) + 手 (te, “hand, hands”) + 上げ (age, “raising”, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 上げる ageru “to raise something”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: さ (sa, “that way”) + も (mo, “even”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Related to the verb 凹む (hekomu, “to become hollow or dented, to collapse inwardly, to sink in”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English interchange.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English elegant.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English style.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English sex.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from French dessin (“a sketch, a drawing”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English pet.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Abbreviation of トランペット (toranpetto, “trumpet”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English PET, itself the initialism for polyethylene terephthalate, a common material used to make plastic.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English range.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “continuative or stem form”) of verb 作る (tsukuru, “to make, to produce, to manufacture”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 兆(きざ)す (kizasu, “to show signs”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from Chinese 免除 (miǎnchú).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 見(め)す (mesu, “(honorific) to see; to govern”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 大(おお) (ō-, “large”) + 幅(はば) (haba, “width, breadth”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 天下 (MC then haeX, “heaven + under”). The kan'on, so likely a later borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 天下 (MC then haeX, “heaven + under”). The go'on, so likely the earlier borrowing.
Appears with this reading in the Kagerō Nikki, dating to roughly 974 CE. Superseded in modern Japanese by tenka above.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally 家礼(けらい) (kerai).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Likely formed from 道(みち) (michi, “path”) + 引(ひ)く (hiku, “to pull; to draw”, rendaku form 引(び)く (biku)), meaning "to pull along a path" -> "to lead/guide".

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Calque of French cadre (“executive, manager”), from 幹(かん) (kan, “core, main part”) + 部(ぶ) (bu, “division, department”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
向 is a daiyōji replacing 嚮.
ikau > ikɔː > ikoː.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨tuwe⟩ → /tuwe/ → /t͡suwe/ → /t͡suje/ → /t͡sue/
From Old Japanese. Found in the Man'yōshū, completed some time after 759 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 杖 (MC drjangX).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 気, air, and 流, current/flow.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 無 (“non-”) + 邪気 (“malice”), attestable in Classical Chinese e.g. Du Fu's famous prose 《秋述》 (literally “autumnal sentiments”) but never as a single word.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 焦(こ)げる (kogeru, “to burn, to blacken”) + 茶(ちゃ) (cha, “(tea) brown”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Alteration of 御 (o-, honorific prefix) + 持ち遊び (mochiasobi, “toy”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/ɡwan ɡu/ → /ɡaŋɡu/
From Middle Chinese 玩具 (MC ngwanH gjuH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 知性 (MC trje sjengH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 耳鼻(じび) (jibi, “ears and nose”) + 科(か) (-ka, “field of study”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *wara.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 蛋白(たんぱく) (tanpaku, “egg white”) + 質(しつ) (-shitsu, “material”); the use of 蛋白 is a semantic loan from German Eiweiß.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Sinicization of 追(お)い放(はな)つ (oihanatsu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 雄 (hjuwng, “male”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wo/ → /o/
From Old Japanese. Persists in compounds, such as the first element o- in the modern Japanese term 夫(おっと) (wohito > otto, “husband”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/wosu/ → /osu/
Compound of 雄 (o, “male”) + す (su), but the derivation of the su element is unknown.
See also the etymology of 雌 (mesu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/won/ → /on/
Compound of 雄 (o, “male”) + ん (n). The latter -n element might be a contraction of the possessive particle の (no).
